import.heading: Import bookmarks from your browser
import.rep.items: Items: %d in the file → %d came into the profile.
import.rep.skippedLead: Another **%d could not come in** (they don't pass the write-path checks; each is listed below).
import.rep.trashedHead: In the browser's own trash (deleted there): %d — **they did not come into the profile**.
import.rep.recOK: **All three checks passed** — what they answer is “did everything that should come in, come in”. They do **not** answer “was anything turned away”, so “all checks passed” and “some bookmarks were left out” can both be true: that list is the “What did not come in” section below.
import.rep.recFail: **Not imported cleanly.** Where the checks failed:
import.rep.slugFallback: - Group titles with no ASCII: %d — their ids fell back to `group-N` (%s). Renaming a title can produce an ASCII id, and the id follows it — **changing an id leaves other people's saved links pointing at nothing**. If you do rename, read this section again afterwards: the new ids are in the list above.
import.rep.slugCollide: - id `%s` collided with “%s”; one of them was renamed.
import.rep.dupTitle: - Same name in %d groups: “%s” — merged into one.
import.rep.checkCount: 1. Item count: should be %d, in the profile %d — %s
import.rep.checkURL: 2. Addresses match: missing %d, appeared out of nowhere %d — %s
import.rep.checkFields: 3. Names and descriptions, one by one: %d mismatched — %s
import.rep.checkNote: Check 3 looks at name and description only: icons **are supposed to differ** (the file has no icon names; they were guessed), which is an allowed tidy-up and is not counted as a failure here.
import.rep.specialsH: What was not copied over (flagged, not auto-fixed)
import.rep.nonHTTPLead: **Not http/https: %d** — a browser won't open those from a page. The URL is kept as it is, and the row gets an “open manually” badge with a copy key:
import.rep.trashed: **In the trash: %d** — you deleted those in the browser already, so they did not come into the profile. They are still in your browser's own bookmarks; if you ever want one back, the browser's trash is faster to search.
import.rep.skippedCountLead: Not imported: %d — with the reason for each:
import.rep.skippedExplain: so the write path refuses them all (`file:` is not in that group: local paths are accepted).
import.rep.emptyGroups: Folders left with nothing inside: %d — none were created (an empty folder in the sidebar just makes people think the import missed something): %s
import.rep.iconGapsLead: Guessed from the address: the host is looked up in the built-in icon index, and **when it isn't found the field is left empty rather than filled with something that looks right** — the latter makes the whole set look iconed until someone checks one by one and finds they are all wrong.
import.rep.iconAdvice: To give one of them an icon: press ✎ on that row and pick in the Icon box, or press “Look up this site's icons” and it queries the built-in index (a name that isn't in it would reject the whole batch, so the box only offers names it can find).
import.explain: A browser bookmark export is one HTML file. Import is open only to a profile with no bookmarks at all, and entries from the browser trash, or addresses that do nothing when clicked such as javascript:, are left out (if one really is left out, the last page names it).
import.notice.blocked: This profile already has %d bookmarks. Import is only open to a profile with none — to add to a list you already have, use the “+ Add” button on the page.
import.notice.unreadable: That upload could not be read. The usual cause is that it is over 8 MB, but a damaged file does it too. Try another one.
import.notice.allSkipped: The bookmarks were read, but none of them can come in — their addresses are javascript: / data: links with no host, the kind a browser won't open from a page either. Keep using those in the browser. (Local file:// paths can be imported.)
import.notice.notABookmarkFile: No bookmarks in this file. Check that it's the .html your browser wrote under Export bookmarks, not a web page saved as HTML.
import.notice.toolarge: That file cannot be read, or it is over 8 MB.
import.notice.noStash: Couldn't stash this upload for the moment — try again in a second.
import.explainStep: A browser export is a single HTML file. In Chrome or Edge: bookmark manager, then the three dots at the top right, then Export bookmarks. In Firefox: Bookmarks, Manage bookmarks, Import and Backup, Export to HTML. What gets imported goes into this profile only.
admin.disable.explain.on: Once disabled, “%s” stays shut even with the right PIN and no longer appears on the picker. Its bookmarks and snapshots do not change at all, and you can enable it again at any time.
admin.disable.explain.off: Once enabled, “%s” can be opened with its PIN again and reappears on the picker.

revert.title: Revert to an earlier version
revert.heading: Revert “%s” to an earlier version?
revert.explain.main: Reverting replaces this profile with the version you picked. Before anything changes, the current state is saved as a snapshot, so a wrong revert can be undone by reverting again. A revert counts as a new change and adds a line to the history; it erases nothing. At most 50 snapshots are kept, and older ones are dropped.
revert.explain.unreadable: A further %d snapshots could not be read and are not listed.
revert.explain.noversions: This profile has no earlier version to revert to yet: one is saved before every change, so right now this is the only version there is.
